responses.content: An adult human has 206 total bones in their body: 27 in the skull, 12 vertebrae in the spine, and various other smaller bones throughout the limbs. The skull specifically contains all of these parts - two small bones at the base (the temporal bone), as well as eight cranial bones that encase and protect the brain: the frontal, parietal (which is a single connected bone but sometimes mentioned individually for clinical purposes), occipital, sphenoid, ethmoid, zygomatic (also known commonly as cheekbones or malar plates - two different names referring to essentially the same structure in this context). Additionally, there are 14 facial bones which include various pairs of small nasal conchae and tiny ear ossicles within each mastoid air cell system.
